oracle_provenance: Wilson (1927) score confidence interval, standard textbook inferential statistics; independently hand-verified before implementation. Not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded statistical-support check for a claimed classification accuracy; not a generalization or deployment-distribution guarantee.

cases.question: Does 95/100 accuracy produce a confidence interval whose lower bound clears an 0.85 minimum?
Does the same 90% point accuracy from only 10 samples fail to clear the same 0.85 minimum, correctly reflecting that small test sets cannot support tight claims?
Must a claimed correct-prediction count exceeding the total be rejected rather than silently used?
At the identical 95% point accuracy, does a much larger test set narrow the confidence interval, discriminating a genuine sample-size effect from noise?
